haiku-low.q1: PRs run build plus unit tests only and never deploy. A merge to main starts the run that can deploy anywhere.
haiku-low.q2: Staging and prod deploy the same image, registry.internal/shop-api:<sha>, built once per run. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration tests retry once. Unit tests never retry. Any test still failing ends the run as failed and posts to #deploys, before staging.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the tag it ran before, via deploy.sh rollback. That tag is found in Parameter Store at /deploy/staging/previous_tag.
haiku-low.q5: Only release-approvers, not the commit author, may approve. If nobody approves within 72 hours, the run expires, prod never gets it, and staging keeps the build.
haiku-low.q6: Tags are in Parameter Store at /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after the main rollout succeeds. Approver details are in the CI run record.
haiku-low.q7: Stable keeps the old tag, since main was never touched and SSM is unchanged. The database keeps the schema the canary migrated, because nothing migrates down.
haiku-low.q8: The older run is cancelled as superseded if it hasn't begun its prod deploy, and a post goes to #deploys.
haiku-low.q9: It waits, polling every 5 minutes, until the Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC window opens and lock P is free. It may finish after 15:00.
haiku-low.q10: The pilot's 5xx share from Prometheus is measured. A job checks once a minute for 15 minutes. Failure is any reading over 1%, or Prometheus returning nothing.
haiku-low.q11: A ping in #deploys tells approvers. It shows IMAGE_TAG, a smoke-results link and the commit list since prod's current_tag. They approve in the CI UI.
haiku-low.q12: A failed stable rollout gets kubectl rollout undo, then canary-off in prod. Not deploy.sh rollback, because SSM isn't written yet and rollback would go one too far back.

sonnet.q1: A PR runs only build plus unit tests (reports PR status) and deploys nothing. A merge to main starts the full run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the same image registry.internal/shop-api:<sha>, built once per run and passed as IMAGE_TAG. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: it is retried once (the 'it again' step). Unit test failure: no retry. Anything still failing ends the run before staging, with a fail post to Slack.
sonnet.q4: deploy.sh rollback staging runs, setting staging back to previous_tag, the tag staging ran before (read from Parameter Store /deploy/staging/previous_tag). The run then fails and posts.
sonnet.q5: Only release-approvers (not the commit author) may approve. If no one approves within 72h of reaching the gate, the run expires and prod never gets it; staging keeps the build. An expired post goes to #deploys.
sonnet.q6: In Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh <env> <tag> writes both, only once the main rollout went fine. The pilot never writes them. For prod, they are written at the stable step.
sonnet.q7: Stable deployment untouched; parameter store still has the old tag; the database keeps whatever migration the canary step ran, since nothing migrates down (the old image has to cope with it).
sonnet.q8: It is cancelled as superseded (kill older), if it hasn't begun its prod deploy (still waiting on sign-off, window, or lock P). A superseded post goes to Slack.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window: it waits, polling every 5 min, until the window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC start only). An approval Thursday evening sits until Monday 09:00 and doesn't lapse. If lock P is held by another prod deploy, it waits the same way.
sonnet.q10: The pilot's (shop-api-canary) 5xx share is measured. The canary-check job asks Prometheus once a minute for 15 minutes. Failure: 5xx share over 1% even once, or Prometheus returns nothing. Then canary-off is run and the run ends.
sonnet.q11: A ping to #deploys (the approval message) carries IMAGE_TAG, a link to the smoke results, and the commit list between prod's current_tag and this tag. People approve in the CI UI.
sonnet.q12: Staging: kubectl rollout undo. Production: kubectl rollout undo, then canary-off, then unlock P. They use this, not deploy.sh rollback, because SSM tags are not written yet, so rollback would go one too far back.
